rows.title: Inchfad distillery
rows.evidence: Wikipedia's Inchfad article says that after the closure of illicit whisky stills around the loch, Inchfad became the home of a registered distillery, and that the MacFarlanes ran a government distillery there until the mid-19th century.
rows.summary: After the closure of illicit whisky stills around the loch, Inchfad became the home of a registered distillery. The ruins can be seen to this day. The MacFarlanes ran a government distillery on the island until the mid-19th century, and a canal on the island was connected with the distillery.

rows.title: Illicit stills on Stroma
rows.evidence: The Stroma article says the islanders concealed illegal distilling by hiding the stills and alcohol in a cave called the Malt Barn, and that illicit distilling continued for many years after smuggling was suppressed.
rows.reject_reason: The article describes illicit distilling and a cave called the Malt Barn, and it never calls the product whisky.
rows.summary: The islanders reportedly concealed illegal distilling from HM Customs and Excise by hiding the stills and alcohol in a cave within The Gloup, called the Malt Barn. While smuggling may have been tackled, illicit distilling continued for many years. A local account says they were distilling and had no time to hide the malt when the excisemen came.

rows.title: Horse Island whiskey distillery
rows.evidence: The Horse Island, County Cork article says that in 2014 an attempt was made to set up an Irish whiskey distillery and visitor centre on the island, but planning permission was refused by An Bord Pleanála. The page coordinates are 51.516, -9.468, the atlas Horse Island off Schull.
rows.reject_reason: Planning permission for a whiskey distillery on the island was refused. The still was not built.
rows.summary: In 2014, an attempt had been made by the Fitzgibbon family to set up an Irish whiskey distillery and visitor centre on the island, but planning permission was refused by An Bord Pleanála.

rows.title: Isle of Cumbrae distillery
rows.evidence: The Isle of Cumbrae distillery article says it is a gin distillery in Millport, Great Cumbrae, and describes gin releases. It does not say the distillery makes whisky.
rows.reject_reason: The distillery's article says it is a gin distillery in Millport and does not describe a whisky still.
rows.summary: Isle of Cumbrae distillery is a gin distillery in Millport, Great Cumbrae, Scotland. The first gin, Nostalgin, was released in September 2020.

rows.title: Illicit poitín on Glashedy
rows.evidence: The Glashedy article says the island was used as a hide-out for making illegally distilled poitín, and that in 1900 police found wash and distilling machinery in a cave which served as a still-house.
rows.reject_reason: The page places poitín distillation on Glashedy. It does not say the spirit was whisky or whiskey.
rows.summary: During the 19th and early 20th century, the island was used as a hide-out for making illegally distilled poitín. In August 1900, police and the coastguard found several hundred gallons of wash and a large quantity of distilling machinery in a cave which served as a still-house.

rows.title: Lussa Gin
rows.evidence: The Jura article says that in 2015 a new distillery was established in Ardlussa at the north of the island, producing Lussa Gin.
rows.reject_reason: The island article places gin production at Ardlussa, not a whisky still. The Jura whisky distillery is already filed.
rows.summary: In 2015 a new distillery was established in Ardlussa at the north of the island, producing Lussa Gin.

rows.title: Deer Island Rum
rows.evidence: The Jura article says that in 2021 the island's first rum distillery opened in Craighouse, producing Deer Island Rum.
rows.reject_reason: The page says this is a rum distillery in Craighouse. Rum does not count.
rows.summary: In 2021 the island's first rum distillery opened in Craighouse producing Deer Island Rum.

rows.title: Lindisfarne Mead
rows.evidence: The Lindisfarne article says Lindisfarne Mead is produced at St Aidan's Winery. It does not describe a whisky still.
rows.reject_reason: The article describes mead from a winery, not a whisky still.
rows.summary: Lindisfarne is well known for mead. Lindisfarne Mead is produced at St Aidan's Winery, and sold widely.
